domain_v2_1.decay_fit_source: results-attempt7-wall-budget-no-plateau/maps.npz, the 400000-step window 2.0-2.4 M steps (3.0-3.6 us); axis column of n_i (window average); the last 0.5 mm before the Dirichlet far plane (phi 44 -> 0 V over ~3.5 lambda_D) excluded from every fit window

axis_profile_measured.note: the axis ion density RISES past the exit to 4.0x the exit value at 27.45 mm (a focus past the axis null at 25.45 mm; the brief's '1.0e18 at 27 mm' is the electron density there: n_e 1.06e18, n_i 2.26e18 at 27.0 mm), then falls: 111 % of the exit value at 30 mm, 72 % at 32, 47 % at 33, 35 % at 34, 22 % at 35, 14.6 % at the far plane 36 mm; electron sample counts per node 1e5-1e6 over the window (well resolved)

axial_decay_fit.power_law: n_i = c (z - z0)^-p with the virtual origin z0 scanned (0-27 mm): best rms 0.041-0.147; z0 = 0 with p = 10-12 on the wide windows (an exponential in disguise), z0 = 21-27 mm with p = 2.35-4.4 on the 31-35.5 / 32-35.5 mm windows (p = 2.35 about z0 = 27 mm is the conical-beam limit n ~ (z - z_focus)^-2 with continuing acceleration); z(10 %) = 37.6-38.6 mm; z(1 %) = 45.6-57.9 mm
axial_decay_fit.result: z10 = 37-39 mm (robust: both families and every window within 1.5 mm; the v2.0 box ends 1-3 mm short of it); z1 = 43-45 mm (exponential family) to 46-58 mm (conical family) - model-dependent by 15 mm because the fit window is 3.5-7.5 mm long and the two families differ only in curvature there
axial_decay_fit.uncertainty_and_bias: the spread across windows and families IS the uncertainty (+-1 mm on z10, 43-58 mm on z1); systematic: the 0 V far plane at 36 mm is inside the acceleration region (the axis potential had 10 % of its drop left at z = 35.8 mm: acceleration_z10_m 0.0358), so the ions are still accelerating at the plane and the measured decay is faster than a free plume's - the extrapolated z10 / z1 are LOWER bounds. A longer box will show a slower tail; the v2.1 record must refit.

radial_extent.half_angle_histogram: j_i(theta) cumulative: 50 % inside 8 deg, 80 % 16 deg, 90 % 29 deg, 95 % 60 deg, 99 % 85 deg. Every crossing above the box corner angle (45 deg) is a SIDE crossing: 6.8 % of the crossings; the side current (0.064 mA) has its median exit at z = 28.1 mm and 37 % within 3 mm of the front face - wide-angle ions from the cone lip / front-face region, not the beam core
radial_extent.at_the_proposed_far_plane: at z_far = 48 mm (24 mm behind the exit) the 90 % cone reaches r = 8.0 mm, the 95 % cone 11.2 mm (inside the 12 mm wall, marginal), the 99 % cone 18.6 mm (side crossing, as at v2.0). Capturing the recorded 95 % half-angle (60 deg) ON the far plane would need r_far = (z_far - 24 mm) tan 60 deg = 24 mm at z10 (38 mm), 35 mm at the exponential z1 (44 mm), 42 mm at 48 mm - a 481-961-row solver (see the cost table) for ions that physically leave sideways at the thruster envelope; R_plume stays 12 mm (the return-yoke radius) and the side tally remains the declared channel for them

domain_v2_1.far_plane_dilution: window-averaged |n_i - n_e| / n_e,peak on candidate planes INSIDE the attempt-7 box (max over resolved nodes, floor 64000 macro-steps): 0.22 at z = 30 mm, 0.12 at 32, 0.08 at 33, 0.06 at 34, 0.038 at 35, 0.028-0.035 at 35.5-36 (the recorded 0.035). Extrapolated with the axis decay to 48 mm: axis n_i 1-3 % of the exit value (6e15-2e16 m^-3) -> a gate quantity of order 0.005-0.01 against the 0.25 threshold, with ~200-400 of the 721 far-field nodes resolved (accumulated weight (n_e + n_i) V_node steps / W >= 64000 for r >= ~0.15 mm at 6e15 m^-3 over 400000 steps). A record whose resolved-node count stays at 0 has an inert gate and must say so.
domain_v2_1.proposal: (z_far, r_far) = (48 mm, 12 mm): L_plume = 24 mm = 1.0 L_channel (2x v2.0; the 1-1.5 L_channel first requested for v2.0 and deferred for lack of FEM coverage), R_plume unchanged. Reaches the 1 % axis point of the exponential family (43-45 mm) with 3-5 mm to spare and sits at 2-4 % under the conical family; the 95 % far-plane current cone fits inside the side wall; uniform 50 um (the solver has no graded spacing, see below); served by the padding-1.5 field without a new FEM solve.

solver_and_mesh_constraints.non_uniform_spacing: NOT supported. Grid2D carries scalar dr_m / dz_m (models.py); mesh.build_mesh_masks builds the finite-volume conductances, shape volumes and charge_to_source from those scalars; kernels.cell_index and every Warp kernel (deposit, gather, push, boundary classification, Courant check, cathode / seed sampling, gate moments) take dr, dz, z_min as scalar arguments (warp_backend.py launches); the frame recorder, dashboards and video renderer assume one node spacing. The CPU BlockTridiagonalSolver and the device WarpBlockThomas themselves only read cond_r / cond_z / diagonal and would accept a graded mesh once the conductances were built for it - the particle side is the work.
solver_and_mesh_constraints.graded_mesh_requirements: (a) Grid2D with node coordinate arrays r_m[i], z_m[j] (piecewise-uniform or geometric) and per-cell dr_i, dz_j; (b) cell_index by piecewise lookup (a mapping table for piecewise-uniform zones keeps it O(1) on the device); (c) bilinear deposit / gather with the local cell size (device arrays of dr_i, dz_j indexed by cell), the charge_to_source ratio per node from the graded shape volumes; (d) Courant gate per cell; (e) frames / maps / dashboards carrying the coordinate arrays; (f) parity tests CPU vs Warp bitwise on a graded tiny box, Poisson manufactured solution and second-order truncation on the graded mesh (the FV operator stays second order only for smooth grading), and the same-seed replay of the uniform case as the regression. Estimated 2-3 days of code + tests; the field solve cost does NOT fall (the sequential block count is the row count, unchanged by z-grading) - grading only saves nodes in the far plume where the particle cost is already small (~4 % of the ions live beyond 33 mm), so the saving is bandwidth on the inverse blocks (m^2 per row) and ~15 % of the node kernels: not worth it at 48 mm.
solver_and_mesh_constraints.channel_only_fine_spacing: a finer dr in the channel only (33 um as v1.x) with 50 um in the plume is a graded-r mesh: the same particle-side work as above plus a row count of 60 + 180 = 240 -> 61 + 180 = 241 (no change in sequential launches) and channel blocks of m = 961; it addresses the peak-Debye margin (3.6 cells/lambda_D at 4.5 gated), not the domain length, and is the natural v2.2 candidate if the peak gate tightens.
solver_and_mesh_constraints.two_domain_approach: channel PIC (v1.4 box, 33 um) coupled to a plume PIC (coarser, 100 um) through the exit plane: requires a particle hand-over buffer with sub-cycled time steps, a matched potential boundary (the exit-plane potential is self-consistent and 75 V above the far plane in attempt 7), two Poisson factorisations, and a conservation ledger across the interface; every v2.0 thrust / momentum ledger and the frame recorder would need the two-grid form. Weeks, not days; only if the plume must reach 60+ mm at 100+ um resolution.
solver_and_mesh_constraints.conclusion: uniform 50 um at 48 x 12 mm is affordable (below) and is the proposal; the graded and two-domain paths are recorded as the fall-backs if a later revision needs z_far >= 60 mm or a wider side wall.

cost_table_v2_1.anchors: attempt 8 (RTX 5090, CUDA-graph step, v2.0.1): 7.0-7.15 ms/step at ~4.4-4.6 M particles (N_e 2.2 M + N_i 2.23 M at 3.78 us, +0.6 M ions/us, 21 % of the ions in the 12 mm plume), GPU 100 %, ~8 GB of 32 GB; 2026-09-03: 4.22 ms/step at 0.55 M; host Schur factorisation of 241 row blocks (721 x 721) ~5 min, 1.0 GB of inverse blocks on the device; host RAM 63 GB total, ~19 GB free with vmmemWSL resident (~30 GB)
cost_table_v2_1.cost_model: ms/step = fixed(grid) + 0.733 ms per M particles (fitted to the two anchors); fixed(241 x 721) = 3.82 ms decomposed as 2 x 241 sequential row-block launches x ~5 us (2.41 ms) + inverse-block reads (nr+1) x 2 x (nz+1)^2 x 8 B = 2.0 GB per solve at ~1.6 TB/s (1.25 ms) + node kernels (0.15 ms); factorisation ~ (nr+1) x (nz+1)^3; device blocks (nr+1) x (nz+1)^2 x 8 B; added plume particles 13k macro per mm (I_beam 0.87 mA / (e x 15 km/s x W 6e4) = 6.5k macro-ions per mm + their electrons); transit = 2.4 us channel residence + L_plume / 17 km/s; 3 transits at dt 1.5 ps
cost_table_v2_1.row_note: the 36 x 12 row is v2.0 (measured, the anchor); the 44 x 12 plume-cell count is the value AFTER the mesh fix (95,820 before it); particles_M is the attempt-8 count plus the added plume, NOT a plateau count: attempt 8 was still adding 0.6 M ions/us, so 6-7 M by 11 us is plausible (+1.5-2 ms/step, +3-4 h to 3 transits) for every row

proposal_48x12.wall_to_3_transits: 17.4 h at 8.2 ms/step (7.62 M steps), ~19.5 h with the particle-count trend, + ~12 min host factorisation per launch/resume; protocol wall budget 79200 s (22 h) so the plateau rule can be evaluated past 3 transits
proposal_48x12.gpu_memory: ~8.8 GB projected (attempt-8 footprint 8.0 + 0.78 GB inverse blocks + ~25 MB node arrays + particle growth) on a 32 GB card that also carries ~5 GB of desktop applications - fits with a wide margin once attempt 8 has released its 8 GB
proposal_48x12.host: factorisation ~12 min (2.37x the measured 5 min), peak host RAM ~1.9 GB for the inverse blocks + temporaries against ~19 GB free with vmmemWSL resident; one factorisation at a time
proposal_48x12.frames: 241 x 961 x float32 x 7 arrays = 6.5 MB/frame uncompressed; 380 frames to 3 transits = 2.5 GB uncompressed, 0.7-1.2 GB at the measured 2-4:1 compression
proposal_48x12.field_map: direct P2 node evaluation over 231,601 nodes (~139k plasma nodes) ~30 s at launch (6 s at v2.0)

cost_table_v2_1.verdict: affordable: +16 % per step and +23 % transit time -> 17-20 h to 3 transits against attempt 8's 14 h budget; NOT prohibitive, so the uniform grid is the proposal and the graded / two-domain alternatives are fall-backs only

field_v2_1.source: modern/spec/pic2d/p2-field-plume-extension-v2.json -> divergent-exit-stack.domain-padding-1.5 (fem_reference qualification chain, phase-matched domain-expansion study at the level-0 resolution; FEM box r <= 48.75 mm, z in [-37.25, 60.75] mm; 61,674 vertices / 122,250 P2 triangles; hash-bound: checkpoint ee3f92e9..., payload 776462f8..., mesh 85c0ce4b..., run e429e3e3..., sidecar 70ee6338...)
field_v2_1.why_not_extrapolate: the far plume field is not negligible for the electrons: level-1 axis |B_z| 16.5 mT at the v2.0 far plane (electron gyroradius 0.3 mm at 2 eV) decaying only as (z - 24 mm)^-0.83 over 28-36 mm; the padded solution gives 14.2 mT at 36 mm, 4.3 at 44, 2.6 at 48, 0.86 at 60 mm ((z - 24)^-2.63 over 36-60 mm). A zero field or a dipole tail beyond 36 mm would have changed the electron transport on the very nodes the plume-boundary gate reads.
field_v2_1.agreement_with_the_qualified_field: channel plasma lattice (r <= 2 mm, z 0.5-23.5 mm): max 0.74 mT, rms 0.35 mT, median relative 0.2 % (max |B| 226 mT); cone/exit (r <= 3 mm, z 18-24): max 0.95 mT; the runner's channel cross-check gate (0.02 T absolute on the channel plasma nodes) passes with 27x margin (1.06 mT on the 60 x 96 coarse test grid)
field_v2_1.truncation_of_the_v2_0_field: on the v2.0 far plane (z = 36 mm, r <= 12 mm) the level-1 and padding-1.5 fields differ by up to 2.4 mT at |B| 16.5 mT (15 %), while padding-1.0 and padding-1.5 agree to 0.38 mT (3 %) beyond 36 mm: the v2.0.x far-plume field carries the level-1 FEM truncation (its boundary sits 0.25 mm behind the PIC far plane). Disclosed for attempts 3-8; one solution over the whole v2.1 domain avoids a seam.
field_v2_1.pole_face_difference: at the pole/yoke corners on the front face (|B| up to 564 mT) the level-0 and level-1 meshes differ by up to 170 mT at single nodes (median relative 2 % over the near plume): a permeable-corner resolution effect both meshes approximate; recorded (field provenance carries the full comparison basis), not gated; the omega_ce dt gate (0.2) is re-evaluated at launch from the run's own map
field_v2_1.identity: field_source = plume-extension-v2, the v2 file's SHA-256, the map declaration and the supported box enter the field provenance -> field_sha256 differs from every v2.0.x map; the v1 extension path produces the v2.0 provenance keys and values bit-for-bit (coarse-grid identity d30d2d24... pinned)

runner_v2_1.resume_state_hygiene: run_steady_state: after loading run_state.json on a resume, _demote_terminal_state moves finished / stop_reason / finalized_from_step / finalization_recovery / finalization_error into run_state.history (one entry per demotion with the event, the step, the UTC time and whether a summary.json of the superseded stop was on disk), sets finished=false, and writes the file BEFORE the first step - a watcher never again reads 'finished: true, stop_reason: wall_clock_budget_reached, finalization_recovery' next to an advancing checkpoint_step (attempt 8's run_state.json, which kept attempt 7's terminal block for its whole session). finalize() applies the same demotion, so a finalized-after-resume run carries its own terminal state and the earlier blocks in history. status() reports finished / stop_reason / history_entries from run_state.json (a resumed run reuses the directory, so a superseded summary.json may sit next to a live checkpoint). Attempt 8's files are untouched: the fix applies to the next resume/finalize executed with this code.

gates_v2_0_3: The prepared v2.1 protocol (experiments/pic2d_cft_plume_v2_1/protocol.json) carries the v2.0.3 gate blocks: peak-Debye gate in window mode (hard pi, soft 2.5, 400000-step window, 40000-step snapshots) and the one-sided windowed residual-power gate (>= 5 % of the electrode work over the trailing 400000 steps) - see pic2d-model-v2.0.json gates_v2_0 (peak_debye_gate_v2_0_3, windowed_energy_residual_gate_v2_0_3, gate_recalibration_history_v2_0_3). The configuration identity changed with the window keys (v2.1 was never launched, so no record is affected). Consequence for the v2.1 decision: at the attempt-8 peak density the 50 um grid reads Delta/lambda_D 3.4-3.8 > pi, so a v2.1 launch on 50 um would now stop at the heating onset (~2.4 us) by design; a resolved plume run needs Delta ~33 um (cost table in the plume v1 README, attempt-8 entry) or a lower operating point.
